- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a 10–15% downward correction to subsequent forecast points.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0) and history shows mean-reverting behavior, model often fails to correct; apply a 0.5–1.0% smoothing factor to forecast mean.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; use 7-day moving average to dampen volatility in forecast tail.
- If sentiment history shows a sudden shift from neutral to positive, model often fails to adjust early; delay peak forecast until 2–3 days after sentiment change.
